title: Admin Dashboard — Real-Time Fixes, Call 404, Conversation UI, Role-Based Auth Flow
summary: Five combined issues: (1) SOS alerts not updating in real-time, (2) driver map pins not updating in real-time, (3) voice/video call buttons redirect to 404, (4) admin-driver chat missing conversation UI, (5) auth flow does not differentiate admin vs driver registration/login or redirect to correct dashboard post-login.

issues.title: SOS alerts and driver map use polling — not real-time
symptoms: New SOS alerts only appear after a page refresh
Driver pin positions on FleetMap only update on the 20-second poll cycle
New drivers coming online do not appear on map until next poll
issues.root_cause: The admin dashboard components fetch data via REST polling intervals instead of subscribing to the existing Ably channels that already broadcast these events in real-time. The SosPanel should subscribe to stress:alerts → stress_signal_alert. The FleetMap should subscribe to user:{adminId} → nearby_driver_update AND listen for a new shared channel for fleet-wide broadcasts.

issues.title: Voice/video call buttons from admin redirect to 404
symptoms: Clicking Voice Call or Video Call on a driver from the admin dashboard results in a 404 page
The call initiate API likely succeeds but the redirect URL is malformed or the call room page does not exist at the expected path
root_cause_hypotheses: The admin dashboard contact buttons navigate to /calls/[roomName] but the call room page lives under app/(protected)/calls/[roomName]/page.tsx which is inside the driver layout group — the admin layout group app/(admin)/ does not include this page, so Next.js cannot resolve it
The navigation after POST /api/calls/initiate uses router.push('/calls/' + roomName) which resolves differently depending on which route group the user is in
The call room page may not exist at all in the admin route group

issues.title: Admin-driver chat has no conversation UI — only a raw message composer modal
symptoms: Admin can send a one-off message via MessageComposerModal but cannot see the conversation history
There is no dedicated conversation thread view for admin
The existing /messages page is inside the driver (protected) layout and not accessible or adapted for the admin role

issues.title: Auth flow does not support role selection — no admin registration or role-based redirect
symptoms: Admin user can only be set by manually running a SQL UPDATE — there is no UI for it
After login, all users are redirected to /dashboard regardless of role
There is no way for an admin to register through the UI
Admins are not automatically redirected to /admin after login

agent_prompt.role: You are a senior full-stack engineer on TruckNet, a Next.js 14 App Router real-time fleet communication platform. Apply all fixes below in the stated order. Every fix must be complete — do not leave TODO comments or placeholder logic.
agent_prompt.objective: Fix all five issues: real-time SOS alerts, real-time driver map, call 404 from admin, admin conversation UI, and role-based auth registration/login/redirect flow.

fix_A.title: Make SOS alerts and driver map fully real-time via Ably

fix_A1_sos_panel.title: SosPanel — subscribe to Ably stress:alerts channel
instructions: Open components/admin/SosPanel.tsx
Import useSocket from hooks/useSocket.ts
Inside the component, call: const { on, off } = useSocket()
Add a useEffect that calls on('stress_signal_alert', handler) where handler receives the new alert payload and prepends it to the local alerts state array using setAlerts(prev => [newAlert, ...prev])

The handler must also: trigger a red pulse animation class on the panel container for 3 seconds, play an alert sound (use a short base64-encoded beep via new Audio()), and update the admin SOS badge count in AdminSidebar via a shared context or by dispatching a custom event
In the useEffect cleanup, call off('stress_signal_alert', handler) to prevent listener leaks
Remove the setInterval polling for SOS alerts entirely — real-time replaces it
Keep the initial fetch (GET /api/admin/sos?status=active) on mount to hydrate the list, then let Ably push updates from that point forward

When the admin resolves an alert via PATCH /api/admin/sos/[id]/resolve, update local state immediately (optimistic update): remove the resolved alert from the active list without waiting for a re-fetch

fix_A2_fleet_map.title: FleetMap — replace polling with Ably real-time driver updates
instructions: Open app/api/drivers/location/route.ts (the POST handler that upserts driver GPS)

After the existing ablyPublish call that sends nearby_driver_update to individual drivers, add a SECOND ablyPublish call that broadcasts to a new shared channel: ablyPublish('fleet:locations', 'driver_location_updated', { userId, name, profileImageUrl, latitude, longitude, updatedAt: new Date().toISOString() })
This fleet:locations channel is public to all admin subscribers and contains live driver movement data
Open components/admin/FleetMap.tsx
Import useSocket and subscribe to the new event inside a useEffect: on('driver_location_updated', handler)

The handler receives { userId, latitude, longitude, updatedAt, name, profileImageUrl } and updates the driver pin in local state: setDrivers(prev => prev.map(d => d.id === userId ? { ...d, latitude, longitude, updatedAt } : d)) — if the userId is not in the list yet (new driver came online), append them: setDrivers(prev => [...prev, newDriver])
Also subscribe to a driver_went_offline event (explained below) to remove pins when drivers go stale
In cleanup, call off('driver_location_updated', handler)
Remove the setInterval polling entirely
Keep the initial GET /api/admin/drivers/live fetch on mount for hydration

In hooks/useSocket.ts, update the SocketProvider useEffect to also subscribe to the fleet:locations channel: const fleetChannel = realtime.channels.get('fleet:locations'); fleetChannel.subscribe('driver_location_updated', dispatch('driver_location_updated')). Add 'fleet:locations' cleanup alongside the existing channel cleanups.

fix_A3_csp_fleet_channel.title: No CSP changes needed — fleet:locations uses the same Ably infrastructure already whitelisted

fix_B.title: Fix voice/video call 404 from admin dashboard
instructions: DIAGNOSIS: The call room page at app/(protected)/calls/[roomName]/page.tsx is inside the driver layout route group. When an admin navigates to /calls/[roomName], Next.js resolves it through the (protected) layout which may redirect the admin away or fail to render because the admin role guard conflicts with the driver layout.
SOLUTION: Create a dedicated call room page inside the admin route group that reuses the exact same LiveKit room component:

STEP 1 — Create app/(admin)/admin/calls/[roomName]/page.tsx. This page must be identical in functionality to the driver call page but rendered inside the admin layout. Copy the full contents of app/(protected)/calls/[roomName]/page.tsx into the new file. The only difference is the file location (route group).

STEP 2 — In all admin contact buttons (AdminDriverCard, FleetMap popup, DriverTable action column), update the post-initiate navigation to use the admin-scoped path: router.push('/admin/calls/' + roomName + '?type=' + callType) instead of router.push('/calls/' + roomName + '?type=' + callType)

STEP 3 — The initiate call flow in admin components must be: (a) call POST /api/calls/initiate with { calleeId: driverId, type: 'voice'|'video' }, (b) await the response to get { roomName, token, liveKitUrl }, (c) store token and liveKitUrl in sessionStorage keyed by roomName so the call page can retrieve them without a second token fetch, (d) router.push('/admin/calls/' + roomName + '?type=' + callType)

STEP 4 — In app/(admin)/admin/calls/[roomName]/page.tsx, on mount read the token from sessionStorage: const token = sessionStorage.getItem('livekit_token_' + roomName). If token is null, fall back to fetching GET /api/calls/[roomName] to get a fresh token. Then call room.connect(liveKitUrl, token).
STEP 5 — After the call ends, navigate back to /admin (not /messages) using router.push('/admin')

fix_C.title: Add full conversation UI for admin-driver messaging
instructions: CREATE app/(admin)/admin/messages/page.tsx — the admin messages landing page. Layout: left panel = AdminConversationList (list of all drivers the admin has conversed with or can message), right panel = AdminConversationThread (the selected thread). This is a two-column layout identical in structure to the driver /messages page.

CREATE components/admin/AdminConversationList.tsx — fetches GET /api/text-messages/conversations (new endpoint, see below) to list all unique conversation partners of the admin user. Renders each as a row: avatar, driver name, tag, last message preview, unread badge, timestamp. Clicking a row navigates to /admin/messages/[driverId] or updates selectedDriverId state (client-side routing within the page).

CREATE components/admin/AdminConversationThread.tsx — accepts driverId prop. Fetches GET /api/text-messages?with={driverId} to load message history. Renders messages as bubbles (AdminMessageBubble). Shows a text input at the bottom with a Send button. On send: POST /api/text-messages { receiverId: driverId, content }. Subscribes to useSocket() on('text_message_received', handler) and appends incoming messages from the selected driver to the thread in real-time WITHOUT a re-fetch.

CREATE components/admin/AdminMessageBubble.tsx — renders a single message bubble. Props: { content, sentAt, isSelf, senderAvatar, senderName }. isSelf = true when senderId === session.user.id. Mirrors the existing driver MessageBubble component styling.

CREATE app/(admin)/admin/messages/[driverId]/page.tsx — deep-link route that pre-selects a specific conversation thread. Used by the View Conversation button on AdminDriverCard. Simply renders the same two-column layout with driverId pre-selected.

MODIFY components/admin/AdminSidebar.tsx — add a Messages nav link pointing to /admin/messages with an unread count badge. The badge count comes from a context or SWR query on GET /api/text-messages/unread-count (reuse or adapt the existing unread count logic from the driver messages page).
MODIFY components/admin/AdminDriverCard.tsx — change the Text Message button from opening MessageComposerModal to navigating to /admin/messages/[driverId]. Delete MessageComposerModal entirely.

ADD GET /api/text-messages/conversations endpoint: returns all unique userIds that the current admin has exchanged messages with, along with the last message and unread count per conversation. Query: SELECT DISTINCT ON (partner_id) ... from text_messages WHERE sender_id = adminId OR receiver_id = adminId ORDER BY created_at DESC.

The real-time subscription in AdminConversationThread must filter incoming text_message_received events by senderId — only append messages to the thread if msg.senderId === the currently viewed driverId, to prevent messages from other drivers appearing in the wrong thread.

fix_D.title: Role-based auth flow — registration with role selection, login with role-based redirect

fix_D1_register.title: Add role selection to registration form
instructions: Open app/(auth)/register/page.tsx

Add a role selector UI element below the existing form fields. Use two large clickable cards (not a dropdown): one card labeled 'Truck Driver' with a truck icon, one card labeled 'Fleet Admin' with a dashboard icon. The selected card gets a highlighted border. Default selection is 'driver'.
The selected role is stored in local component state: const [role, setRole] = useState<'driver' | 'admin'>('driver')
Include the role in the form submission payload to POST /api/auth/register: { name, email, password, role }
Update the Zod UserRegisterSchema in schemas/user.schema.ts to include: role: z.enum(['driver', 'admin']).default('driver')

Open app/api/auth/register/route.ts and update the INSERT to include the role field from the validated body: db.insert(users).values({ ...validatedData, role: body.role ?? 'driver', passwordHash, tag, tagNumber })

SECURITY NOTE: In a production app, admin registration should require an invite code or be disabled publicly. Add an optional adminInviteCode field to the register schema. If role === 'admin', validate that the submitted code matches env.ADMIN_INVITE_CODE. If the code is wrong or missing, return 403. Add ADMIN_INVITE_CODE to env.schema.ts and .env.local. This prevents anyone from self-registering as admin.

fix_D2_login_redirect.title: Role-based redirect after login
instructions: Open auth.ts (the full Auth.js config with Credentials provider)
In the callbacks.jwt callback, after the existing user data is added to token, add: if (user?.role) token.role = user.role
In the callbacks.session callback, add: if (token?.role) session.user.role = token.role as 'driver' | 'admin'
Update the TypeScript type declarations in types/next-auth.d.ts (or next-auth.d.ts at root): extend the Session.user type with role: 'driver' | 'admin'
Open middleware.ts — find the authorized() callback or the redirect logic that runs after successful authentication

Add a post-login redirect based on role: if the user's role is 'admin' and they are on /login or /register or /, redirect them to /admin. If their role is 'driver', redirect to /dashboard. Specifically: in the Auth.js authorized callback, if (token?.role === 'admin' && request.nextUrl.pathname === '/') return Response.redirect(new URL('/admin', request.url))
Also handle the case where an admin manually visits /dashboard — redirect them to /admin instead
And where a driver manually visits /admin/* — redirect them to /dashboard

The complete redirect matrix in middleware.ts must be: (1) unauthenticated → /login, (2) authenticated driver on / or /dashboard → /dashboard (existing behavior), (3) authenticated admin on / or /login or /dashboard → /admin, (4) authenticated driver on /admin/* → /dashboard with toast, (5) authenticated admin on driver-only paths → allowed (admin has broader access)

fix_D3_login_page_ux.title: Update login page to inform users about role-based access
instructions: Open app/(auth)/login/page.tsx
The login form itself does NOT need a role selector — role is stored in the database and retrieved on authentication automatically
Add a subtle info line below the submit button: 'Admins will be redirected to the fleet dashboard automatically.'

After successful signIn(), do NOT manually call router.push('/dashboard') — instead call router.push('/') and let the middleware handle the role-based redirect. This ensures the correct destination for both drivers and admins.
Remove any hardcoded router.push('/dashboard') calls in the login form onSubmit handler and replace with router.push('/')

fix_E.title: New environment variable for admin invite code
instructions: Add ADMIN_INVITE_CODE to schemas/env.schema.ts: ADMIN_INVITE_CODE: z.string().min(8).optional()
Add it to lib/env.ts export
Add ADMIN_INVITE_CODE=your-secret-code-here to .env.local

In app/api/auth/register/route.ts, when role === 'admin': if (!body.adminInviteCode || body.adminInviteCode !== env.ADMIN_INVITE_CODE) { return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Invalid admin invite code' }, { status: 403 }); }
In the registration UI, when role === 'admin' is selected, show an additional input field: 'Admin Invite Code' with type='password'. This field is hidden when role === 'driver'.

new_api_route.description: Returns all unique conversation partners for the current user (used by admin conversation list and could benefit driver messages too). For each partner returns: partnerId, partnerName, partnerAvatar, partnerTag, lastMessage { content, createdAt, isSelf }, unreadCount.

query_logic: Select all messages where sender_id = userId OR receiver_id = userId
Group by the other participant (CASE WHEN sender_id = userId THEN receiver_id ELSE sender_id END as partner_id)
For each partner: get the most recent message (ORDER BY created_at DESC), get count of messages where receiver_id = userId AND status = 'delivered'
JOIN users on partner_id to get name, tag, profileImageUrl
Return sorted by last message created_at DESC

verification_steps.action: Open /admin dashboard. Trigger a stress signal from a driver account in another browser tab. Verify the SOS alert appears in SosPanel within 1-2 seconds WITHOUT refreshing the admin page.
Open /admin dashboard. Move a driver (update their GPS via POST /api/drivers/location from a driver account). Verify the driver pin on FleetMap moves within 2 seconds WITHOUT refreshing.

Click Voice Call on any driver from the admin dashboard FleetMap popup or DriverTable. Verify it navigates to /admin/calls/[roomName] (not /calls/[roomName]) and the LiveKit room connects successfully with no 404.
Click Video Call from the admin dashboard. Verify same — navigates to /admin/calls/[roomName]?type=video and connects.

Navigate to /admin/messages. Verify the conversation list loads. Click a driver. Verify the message thread loads with history. Send a message. Verify the driver receives it in real-time on their /messages page.
Send a text message FROM a driver TO the admin. Verify the admin's conversation thread updates in real-time without refresh.
Register a new account with role='driver'. Verify after login they are redirected to /dashboard.
Register a new admin account using the correct ADMIN_INVITE_CODE. Verify after login they are redirected to /admin.
Try to register as admin with a wrong invite code. Verify the API returns 403 and the form shows an error.
Log in as an admin and manually navigate to /dashboard. Verify middleware redirects to /admin.
Log in as a driver and manually navigate to /admin. Verify middleware redirects to /dashboard.

constraints: The fleet:locations Ably channel must be added to the CSP connect-src in next.config.mjs — it uses the same Ably domains so no new domain entries are needed, but verify the channel name does not conflict with existing topology
sessionStorage used to pass LiveKit tokens to the admin call page must be cleaned up after use: sessionStorage.removeItem('livekit_token_' + roomName) after the room connects
The admin conversation thread real-time listener must be scoped to the currently viewed driverId — do not append messages from other drivers to the wrong thread
The role field in the JWT and session must use the value from the database — never trust a client-supplied role claim
ADMIN_INVITE_CODE must be at least 16 characters in production and must never be committed to git

The /admin/calls/[roomName]/page.tsx must reuse the exact same LiveKit room logic as the driver call page — do not duplicate the WebRTC logic, extract it into a shared component at components/calls/CallRoomView.tsx that both pages import
Removing MessageComposerModal must not break any existing imports — search the codebase for all usages before deleting
The role-based middleware redirect must not create redirect loops — add a check that the user is not already on the correct destination before redirecting
